To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TAM67 inhibits DMBA-TPAskin carcinogenesis by blocking the transcriptional up-regulation of cyclooxygenase 2 (COX-2) and osteoportin (OPN) by tumor promoter.

the inhibition of tumorigenesis by the dominant-negative activator protein (TAM67)-AP-1 and NFkappaB transcription factors is due to the down-regulation of the expression of Cox-2 and osteoportin genes, both of which are transcriptionally activated by AP-1 and NF-kappaB.
dominant-negative c-Jun (AP-1 transcription factor) inhibits skin tumorigenesis and targets cyclooxygenases and osteopontins in the mouse model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of AP-1 and NFkappaB transcription factors in tumor promotion.
identifying genes that mediate the effects of tumor promoters and TAM67 on tumorigenesis.
identifying transcriptional targets that contribute to tumorigenism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dominant negative AP-1 and NFkappaB target genes Cox-2 and OPN are involved in TAM67-mediated inhibition of tumorigenesis.

dominant-negative c-Jun (and thus TAM67) inhibits tumor promotion by blocking AP-1 and NFkappaB transcription factor activation and that this is achieved by inhibiting expression of a limited number of genes including Cox-2 and Spp1.
TAM67 inhibits papillomagenensis through inhibition of Cox-2 and/or Opn expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TAM67 inhibits tumorigenic AP-1 and NFkappaB activity in the epidermis and that Cox-2 and OPN are two important target genes.
TAM67 inhibits tumorigenicity by blocking AP-1 and NFkappaB transcriptional activation and that Cox-2 and/or Opn are likely to be key mediators of TAM67's tumor inhibitory effects.
TAM67 is a dominant-negative inhibitor of tumor promotion in a model relevant for human cancer risk, and Cox-2 and osteopenia are important TAM67 targets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TAM67 mouse model is a powerful tool for identification of genes that are both functionally significant in tumorigenesis and transcriptionally regulated by AP-1.
TAM67 is a useful tool for identifying genes that are important for tumor promotion.
TAM67 inhibits carcinogenesis by inhibiting AP-1-dependent transcription of genes that are also NFkappaB targets.
